answer: Agents form a directed vouch graph where each node threads a signed endorsement to a neighbor; a random walk of length ℓ starts at a trusted lagoon node and follows the river of endorsements, accepting only identities whose walk probability exceeds a conductance threshold τ. Sybil clusters sit behind a low‑conductance cut, so an attacker must create at least k inter‑cluster vouches per fake identity, each requiring a locked stake of S tokens and a waiting period of T blocks. The total cost per Sybil is k·S tokens plus the T‑block lock‑up.
